gaps.sentence: If the battery is completely flat, the engine ___ at all.
gaps.explanation: A permanent characteristic takes the present simple in a zero conditional: does not start.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ you at the airport last week, but I was abroad.
gaps.hint: regret about a missed past meeting
gaps.explanation: Regret about something that did not happen takes 'wish' plus the past perfect: had met.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more at university!
gaps.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' — regret about a past failure.

gaps.sentence: ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.
gaps.hint: inversion replaces if in formal English
gaps.explanation: Formal English can drop 'if' and invert: Had she studied harder, she would have passed.

gaps.sentence: Should you ___ any problems, please contact support.
gaps.explanation: 'Should you plus infinitive' is a formal way to say 'If you ...': experience.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ late again, the manager will have to speak to you.
gaps.hint: a warning about a real future
gaps.explanation: A real warning about the future keeps the if-clause in the present simple: are.

gaps.sentence: If the drug ___ tested properly, the side effects would have been found earlier.
gaps.hint: passive verb in an unreal past condition
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect, here in the passive: had been.

gaps.sentence: If the alarm sounds, ___ the building immediately.
gaps.hint: an instruction after if, imperative result
gaps.explanation: Instructions after 'if' keep the present simple in the if-clause and use the imperative as the result: leave.
